Based. Human creation / taste / judgment has very rewarding after effects and RL data has to be the domain which leverages the most of it.

Even synthesising a repo for useful task generation comes with a LOT of judgement effects. It could be your 
> authenticity
> task-ability
> difficulty calibration
> business relevance
> context sufficiency
and so many other integral factors.

For someone to consume this data/task to hillclimb a model behaviour, the human expertise layer is often where much of the value is created.

Ask The AI How To Ask The AI
> Trying something AI can't do costs you thirty seconds.
> Skipping something it could have done costs you the entire task, silently, forever.
> That asymmetry decides how much you get out of the machine.
> The gap between light and power AI users isn't skill, it's reflex
> Power users have collapsed the latency between "I have a problem" and "I could hand this to AI" to near zero, while most people's sense of what AI can do freezes at their first impression and never updates.
